chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the meal is presented, if one man from them mentions the name of God (says Bismillah), it suffices for all of them.'
ai.seo_question: Does one person need to say Bismillah for everyone else when eating together?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the fiqh of communal dining by establishing that a single *Bismillah* recited by one participant suffices for the entire group, reflecting the principle of shared blessing in a unified setting. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between individual obligations and collective acts of worship, emphasizing unity during meals. It underscores the ease Islam places on social gatherings, provided the essential invocation is present.
